faqs.questions: How to login on Investor Web?

faqs.answers: You can visit the hamburger menu & click on "Fund Transfer" to find "Add Funds" menu. Post clicking on "Add Funds", you can transfer the required amount through Net Banking & UPI. Funds if successfully transferred will get reflect in your trading account immediately.

faqs.questions: How to intra transfer funds from 1 segment to another?

faqs.questions: How to withdraw funds online?

faqs.questions: Can I create a pre-defined index watchlist?

faqs.questions: How to view the mini get quote page of Watchlist?

faqs.questions: What is Margin Trading Facility (MTF)?
faqs.answers:
Margin Trading Facility (MTF) allows an investor to buy a stock by paying just a fraction of the total transaction value. The balance amount is funded by the broker.
As an illustration:
Your Account Balance = Rs. 25,000
MTF gives you upto 4x buying power = Rs 100,000 (25,000 x 4)
Thus, your enhanced Buying Capacity is now = Rs. 125,000.

faqs.questions: What is the Interest rate charged to use MTF?
faqs.answers: A Standard Interest rate of 0.053% per day (19.5% per annum) is charged on the borrowed amount.

faqs.questions: How long can I hold the stocks purchased via MTF?
faqs.answers: You can hold your positions under MTF as long as you maintain the required margin in your account.

faqs.questions: When will I start incurring interest charges?
faqs.answers: Interest is levied from the 2nd day onwards after you placed an MTF trade, till the outstanding amount is cleared, and/or your position is squared-off.

faqs.questions: What is MTF Pledge?
faqs.answers:
MTF Pledge is a mandatory process introduced by SEBI.
When you buy shares under Margin Trading Facility, you will have to pledge those shares to continue holding the position.
This process must be completed by 9 pm on the same day. In case you fail to do so, your shares will be squared-off on T+7 day.

faqs.questions: How do I pledge my shares for Margin Trading Facility?
faqs.answers:
After placing a trade using Margin Trading Facility, you will receive a link from CDSL on your registered Email ID & SMS for authentication after 5:30 pm on T-day (Trade Day)
This link will be valid till 9 pm on T day
Upon visiting the link enter your PAN number & authenticate the transaction using OTP
On successful validation pledge will be created & you will receive an intimation on your registered email ID & mobile number.

Alternatively, you can directly visit the CDSL website & pledge your shares after 5:30 pm. Below is the Margin Trading Pledge link for CDSL.  
https://www.cdslindia.com/Authentication/OTP.aspx

faqs.questions: What is Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: Dematerialisation is conversion of physical shares in electronic form.

faqs.questions: How to give request for Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: Get duly filled and signed Dematerialisation Request Form (DRF) along with physical certificates from the client, deface the certificates and upload the scan of all documents along with data entry in CBOS for Pre-approval. Once Pre-approved, send documents to HO.

faqs.questions: How to get a DRF?
faqs.answers: The new pre-printed CDSL ‘DRF’ and ‘Mutual Fund DRF’ can be downloaded from Bizops, the path is given below: Bizops => Information => Download Forms For NSDL DRF, both Equity & MF, send mail along with DP ID and Address of BA/Branch to <redacted>

faqs.questions: Is DRF for Equity and Mutual Fund different?
faqs.answers: Yes. The DRF for Equity is called ‘Dematerialisation Request Form’ (DRF) and that for Mutual Fund is called ‘MF - Dematerialisation Request Form’ (MF – DRF).

faqs.questions: What is the checklist to process DRF at BA/Branch?
faqs.answers: The branch official should verify the following prior to entry of DRF in back office: a. DRF is filled completely in all respects and signed by all the holders of the account. b. Correction or overwriting on DRF, if any, must be authenticated by all the holders. White ink should not be used on correction or any other part of DRF. c. The DRF must be signed & stamped with round stamp of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd..by the authorized branch DP person. d. In case of Mutual Fund (MF), latest Statement of Account (SOA) duly signed by client on all pages, should be attached. e. The branch has to deface certificates by affixing the rubber stamp in the prescribed format (“Surrender for dematerialization” stamp along with DP Name, DP ID and Client ID), punching two holes on the Company Name and striking two parallel lines across the certificates. f. Transposition Form should be attached in case of change in sequence of Joint holders, in Certificates and DP Account. The sequence in DRF should be as per DP account. g. Transmission-cum-Demat Form along with original or notarized copy of death certificate of the deceased holder, if any, to be attached.

faqs.questions: What are the charges for Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: The charges for dematerialisation are Rs.50/- per DRF, Rs.50/- for each Certificate and Rs.50/- towards Courier charges.

faqs.questions: Where to punch the request for Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers:
The path for the module is given below:

CBOS > Demat > DP Module > Demat & Remat-CDSL > +Add New

faqs.questions: What is Transposition-cum-Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers:
For the dematerialisation of physical shares the name of  holder(s) on the certificates as well as in the demat account should be the same and also in same  sequence. In  event  of  change in the  sequence  of  the  name  of  the  holders,  the  shares  can  be dematerialised  provided a Transposition form duly filled and signed by all the holders  is  submitted along with the DRF.

This is called the Transposition-cum-Dematerialisation.
Format of Transposition form is available in:

Bizops >Information > Downloads (DP) > Transposition Form NEW

faqs.questions: What is Transmission-cum-Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers:
If one or more holders of a Joint Account has deceased, the dematerialisation of physical share can be done by accompanying Death Certificate(s) (original or notarized) and Transmission-cum-Dematarialisation Form along with DRF and Certificates.

This is called the Transmission-cum-Dematerialisation.
Format of the Transmission-cum-Dematarialisation Form is available in:

Bizops > information > Downloads (DP) > Transmission Process and Formats

faqs.questions: Where to view the status of the request for Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: The status can be viewed in any of the below mentioned reports: a. Maker Checker Report  b. DIS/DRF/Pledge Status Report (Formerly Instruction Verification Status Report)

faqs.questions: When should the physical original documents to be sent?
faqs.answers: All the physical original documents like DRF, Certificates, etc. should be sent to HO only after the DRF request is ‘pre-approved’ in back office.

faqs.questions: Where should the physical documents be sent?
faqs.answers: The documents has to be sent to the below mentioned address by generating packet no. through HiTs: The Depository Department (DP) Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. 2nd Floor, Palm Court Complex, Palm Spring Centre, Link Road, Malad (West), Mumbai – 400 064. Ph: 022 7188 1000/01

faqs.questions: What is the TAT for Pre-approval?
faqs.answers: The TAT for Pre-approval is T day with a cut-off of 4 pm, ie. all requests received up to 4 pm in back office at HO, are processed on the same day.

faqs.questions: What is the TAT for sending the shares to RTA for dematerialisation by DP?
faqs.answers: The TAT as per the regulatory guidelines is T+7 days from receipt of DRF and Share certificate at HO. However, the shares are sent to RTA by next working day by MOFSL DP.

faqs.questions: What is the TAT followed by RTA for dematerialisation / destatementisation?
faqs.answers: The TAT of RTA for dematerialisation / destatementisation is 15 working days.

faqs.questions: What should be done in case of objection in the request for dematerialisation?
faqs.answers:
Go to CBOS > Demat > DP Module > Demat & Remat-CDSL
1Double Click on the respective DRF No.
2 Check Rejection Details
3 If rectifiable, rectify the observations. Overwrite the revised documents, if any.
4 Save ‘Securities Details’ and ‘Attachments’
5 Click on Submit

faqs.questions: The Physical rejected DRF by HO or RTA are sent to whom?
faqs.answers: The documents are sent directly to client’s registered address only by the DP as per regulatory guidelines. It cannot be sent to BA or Branch.

faqs.questions: When will  the client get the shares rejected by HO or RTA?
faqs.answers: The shares rejected by HO, are returned to Client, by next working day.The shares rejected by RTA are sent to Client by T+3 working day from the receipt of shares from RTA.

faqs.questions: What are the major reasons for rejections in Pre-approval of DRF?
faqs.answers: Some of the major reasons for rejections in Pre-approval are: a. Signature mismatch with DP records b. DRF incompletely filled Refer our Circular titled DRF Common Observations dated 26th May 2022. Click here for the circular

faqs.questions: What are the major reasons for rejections of Physical DRF by HO?
faqs.answers: Some of the major reasons for rejections of Physical DRF are: a. The old defunct shares received instead of new shares (Not attached in pre-approval) b. Rejections from CDSL

faqs.questions: What are the major reasons for rejections of DRF by RTA?
faqs.answers: The major reasons for rejections by RTA are: a. Signature mismatch with RTA records b. Incorrect Holder Name pattern c. Address mismatch in RTA records

faqs.questions: What does the rejection reason ‘Invalid Holding Type For - Of’ from CDSL mean?
faqs.answers: As per CDSL, ‘Invalid Holding Type For - Of’ means any one of the reason from the following list. The exact reason can be explained by RTA only. Client have to check with RTA only. a. Client may not have claimed dividend for more than 7 years b. Address may be mismatch in CDSL record and RTA record c. Type of holding is different d. Might be old share e. Share certificate is already in demat.

faqs.questions: What are the below mentioned CDSL rejections?
faqs.answers: DN Ranges Not Found In Static Database. DNR Ranges Not Found in DN Database. The above mentioned reasons are due to the Distinctive Numbers not present in CDSL database. Please check the Distinctive Numbers in the CDSL database, before processing the DRF. If the Distinctive Numbers shows in the CDSL database, you may process the DRF, else kindly return the DRF to the client. Click here for the Process to check Distinctive Numbers in CDSL database.Refer our Circular dated 28th October 2021, titled DRF Rejections. Click here for the Circular.

faqs.questions: What is Destatementisation?
faqs.answers: Destatementisation is the process, which enables Beneficiary Owners (BOs) to convert their mutual fund units represented by Statement of Account (SOA) in physical form to electronic form and hold the same in their demat account with CDSL.

faqs.questions: What is SOA and for which period the same is to be submitted?
faqs.answers: SOA is ‘Statement of Account’ in case of Mutual Fund transaction, which needs to be attached along with MF DRF. The statement of last 3 months, having ISIN,  is required.

faqs.questions: What quantity should be filled for MF unit dematerialisation in MF DRF?
faqs.answers: To avoid rejection from RTA, please write “ALL” in both the Quantity column in MF DRF, irrespective of the quantity mentioned in statement of account. However, specific number of units should be mentioned in case of lock-in units.

faqs.questions: Is single DRF sufficient for free as well as lock-in securities/MF units?
faqs.answers: No. Separate DRF needs to be given for securities/units with different Lock-in release dates and also for Free and Lock-in securities/units.

faqs.questions: Whether physical Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) certificate can be dematerialized?
faqs.answers: No. The client has to co-ordinate with the Issuer Bank for the same.

faqs.questions: Whether Warrants can be dematerialized?
faqs.answers: No.

faqs.questions: Whether Bonds and Debentures can be dematerialized?
faqs.answers: Yes, if the ISIN is available for demat.

faqs.questions: What is a DIS and why is it required
faqs.answers:
DIS  is  a  Delivery  Instruction  Slip.  It  is  required to transfer shares from one demat account to another demat account just like a cheque is used to transfer funds from 
  one bank account to another bank account.

faqs.questions: How many slips are there in a DIS book sent by DP?
faqs.answers: There are 10 slips in a DIS book sent by DP

faqs.questions: What are the charges for a DIS Book?
faqs.answers: Rs. 50/- is charged as on date (Nov’22) for a DIS book. Additionally, there is a courier charge of Rs.50/- per book The DIS book charges can be checked in: CBOS è DP Module è Views and Reports è Dp Detailed Bill Report

    clients) is by sending just an SMS from the registered SMS Mobile Number of the  
    client  to  our  designated Number <redacted>, in the below format. If SMS is sent
    from an unregistered SMS Mobile number, it will not be processed.

    CDIS<space><16 digit BO ID> 

    Example: CDIS 1201090000002345 (CDSL Client)
CDIS IN30297810416309 (NSDL Client–DP ID IN302978 + Client ID
                                             10416309) 
Note: For NSDL Clients,  this  facility  is  only  for  domestic  Individual account 
   holder, held singly. Individual NRI, PMS, Joint holders and Non-Individual clients
   have to use Physical mode of request only, which is mentioned below.
b. In case of any technical issue in sending the SMS, the client can give the request  
using a DIS Requisition Slip available in existing DIS book with the client, if any.
 c. If  both  a & b  is  not possible, the client can give the request by DIS Requisition  letter.

Click on the below links for the formats of the letter:
DIS Book Requisition letter_CDSL_14.09.2022
DIS Book Requisition letter_NSDL_14.09.2022
 These are available in Bizops login also, the path of which is given below:
BizopsàInformationàDownloadsàDIS Request Letter Format – CDSL & NSDL

faqs.answers:

 mobile number from which the request is sent, in case of successful SMS request.
 In case of unsuccessful SMS request, an error message is received immediately

 * Date should be the same as the date on which request is raised in back office.

faqs.questions: What details are required in DIS Requisition Letter

faqs.questions: What are the common rejection reasons in DIS Requisition Slip?
faqs.answers:
Ø  Date not mentioned on the Slip
Ø  Date in the Slip differs from the date on which request is raised in back office.
Ø  Signature of Sole holder or any or all of the joint holder’s differs

faqs.questions: What are the common rejection reasons in DIS Requisition Letter?
faqs.answers:
Ø  Date not mentioned on the Letter
Ø  Date in the Letter differs from the date on which request is raised in back office.
Ø  Demat Account Number not mentioned or wrongly mentioned
Ø  Signature of Sole holder or any or all of the joint holder’s differs

faqs.questions: What precautions must be taken by the Client for an SMS request
faqs.answers:
The client needs to ensure that:

faqs.questions:

      clients while punching in back office?

      months. A  pop-up  alert  is  displayed  in  back office  while punching DIS requests for 
      such clients to give alert to BA to ensure and check the credibility and genuineness of 
      the DIS.

 Six months.

faqs.questions: When the shares will get transferred to target account after DIS execution process is done by DP?
faqs.answers: After the DIS is executed by DP, the instructions will be uploaded in CDSL in batches. The client has to click on the link, verify the details of the transactions and  Generate an OTP. An OTP will be received on client’s registered SMS mobile  number  and  Email ID, which has to be entered and submitted. This is called OTP  authentication process and is  mandatory  for  shares  transfer. Once this process is done, shares will get tranferred to the counter client account. If  this  process  is  not done by the client, shares will not get transferred even if the process is completed by DP.

faqs.questions: Can NRI/PIO invests in other securities?

faqs.answers: No, NRI Investor has to take delivery of shares purchased and give delivery of shares sold. Short Selling is not permitted

faqs.questions: Can NRI trade in Currency derivative segment of the Exchange?
faqs.answers: No, Only “a person resident in India” as defined in section 2(v) of FEMA Act 1999 are allowed to participate in currency derivative segment of the Exchange

faqs.questions: In case a non-resident Indian becomes a resident in India, will he/she be required to change the status of his/her holding from Non-Resident to Resident
faqs.answers: Yes. The ageing can be reduced by way of cheque collection or only selling of position.

faqs.questions: Margin and Margin Reporting under interoperability?
faqs.answers: As per the Clarification given by NSE on their circular dated 16th May 2019 the margin reporting will be done on combined basis. WE shall consider the consolidated ledger balance across all segments (excluding balance in the clientâ€™s Margin Trading (MTF) account) and Exchange for the purpose of collection & reporting Margin/MTM losses of the client. The debit or credits ledger in all segment clubbed together (including CASH Commodities FNO and Currency). Also will consider the collateral across all segment (i.e stocks lying in Debit stock of Cash segments collateral stocks POA stocks Cash collateral FD and BGs after appropriate haircut). The priority for Margin reporting will be as follows: Currency FNO MCX NCDEX NSE Commodities BSE commodities. If the customer have debit in cash segment and taken position in FNO while margin reporting the debit in cash segment will also be considered towards margin reporting and penalties will be levied in case of shortage. You are requested to take proper care while shifting any FNO/Currency/Commodity positions.

faqs.questions: Will the reporting under Margin Trading (MTF) change due to interoperability?
faqs.answers: Reporting shall be done on the Exchange on which the exposure was taken (i.e. scrip was bought). However in case of liquidation the reporting shall be done on the Exchange in which the scrip was bought under the column provided for liquidation even if it was liquidated on another Exchange.

faqs.questions: What is Margin Trading Facility (MTF)?
faqs.answers:
Margin Trading Facility (MTF) allows an investor to buy a stock by paying just a fraction of the total transaction value. The balance amount is funded by the broker.
As an illustration:
Your Account Balance = Rs. 25,000
MTF gives you upto 4x buying power = Rs 100,000 (25,000 x 4)
Thus, your enhanced Buying Capacity is now = Rs. 125,000.

faqs.questions: What is the Interest rate charged to use MTF?
faqs.answers: A Standard Interest rate of 0.053% per day (19.5% per annum) is charged on the borrowed amount.

faqs.questions: How long can I hold the stocks purchased via MTF?
faqs.answers: You can hold your positions under MTF as long as you maintain the required margin in your account.

faqs.questions: When will I start incurring interest charges?
faqs.answers: Interest is levied from the 2nd day onwards after you placed an MTF trade, till the outstanding amount is cleared, and/or your position is squared-off.

faqs.questions: What is MTF Pledge?
faqs.answers:
MTF Pledge is a mandatory process introduced by SEBI.
When you buy shares under Margin Trading Facility, you will have to pledge those shares to continue holding the position.
This process must be completed by 9 pm on the same day. In case you fail to do so, your shares will be squared-off on T+7 day.

faqs.questions: How do I pledge my shares for Margin Trading Facility?
faqs.answers:
After placing a trade using Margin Trading Facility, you will receive a link from CDSL on your registered Email ID & SMS for authentication after 5:30 pm on T-day (Trade Day)
This link will be valid till 9 pm on T day
Upon visiting the link enter your PAN number & authenticate the transaction using OTP
On successful validation pledge will be created & you will receive an intimation on your registered email ID & mobile number.

Alternatively, you can directly visit the CDSL website & pledge your shares after 5:30 pm. Below is the Margin Trading Pledge link for CDSL.  
https://www.cdslindia.com/Authentication/OTP.aspx

faqs.questions: What is Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: Dematerialisation is conversion of physical shares in electronic form.

faqs.questions: Is DRF for Equity and Mutual Fund different?
faqs.answers: Yes. The DRF for Equity is called ‘Dematerialisation Request Form’ (DRF) and that for Mutual Fund is called ‘MF - Dematerialisation Request Form’ (MF – DRF).

faqs.questions: What is the checklist to process DRF at BA/Branch?
faqs.answers: The branch official should verify the following prior to entry of DRF in back office: a. DRF is filled completely in all respects and signed by all the holders of the account. b. Correction or overwriting on DRF, if any, must be authenticated by all the holders. White ink should not be used on correction or any other part of DRF. c. The DRF must be signed & stamped with round stamp of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd..by the authorized branch DP person. d. In case of Mutual Fund (MF), latest Statement of Account (SOA) duly signed by client on all pages, should be attached. e. The branch has to deface certificates by affixing the rubber stamp in the prescribed format (“Surrender for dematerialization” stamp along with DP Name, DP ID and Client ID), punching two holes on the Company Name and striking two parallel lines across the certificates. f. Transposition Form should be attached in case of change in sequence of Joint holders, in Certificates and DP Account. The sequence in DRF should be as per DP account. g. Transmission-cum-Demat Form along with original or notarized copy of death certificate of the deceased holder, if any, to be attached.

faqs.questions: What are the charges for Dematerialisation?
faqs.answers: The charges for dematerialisation are Rs.50/- per DRF, Rs.50/- for each Certificate and Rs.50/- towards Courier charges.

In  event  of  change in the  sequence  of  the  name  of  the  holders,  the  shares  can  be dematerialised  provided a Transposition form duly filled and signed by all the holders  is  submitted along with the DRF.

This is called the Transposition-cum-Dematerialisation.
Format of Transposition form is available in:

Bizops >Information > Downloads (DP) > Transposition Form NEW

This is called the Transmission-cum-Dematerialisation.
Format of the Transmission-cum-Dematarialisation Form is available in:

faqs.questions: What is Destatementisation?

faqs.questions: Margin and Margin Reporting under interoperability?
faqs.answers: As per the Clarification given by NSE on their circular dated 16th May 2019 the margin reporting will be done on combined basis. WE shall consider the consolidated ledger balance across all segments (excluding balance in the clientâ€™s Margin Trading (MTF) account) and Exchange for the purpose of collection & reporting Margin/MTM losses of the client. The debit or credits ledger in all segment clubbed together (including CASH Commodities FNO and Currency). Also will consider the collateral across all segment (i.e stocks lying in Debit stock of Cash segments collateral stocks POA stocks Cash collateral FD and BGs after appropriate haircut). The priority for Margin reporting will be as follows: Currency FNO MCX NCDEX NSE Commodities BSE commodities. If the customer have debit in cash segment and taken position in FNO while margin reporting the debit in cash segment will also be considered towards margin reporting and penalties will be levied in case of shortage. You are requested to take proper care while shifting any FNO/Currency/Commodity positions.
